name: desire for environment knowledge
quote: I'd like to know what's going on.
description: Wanting to better understand the physical or social environment towards making better decisions about them.

variations.name: first party social knowledge
variations.description: Wanting to better understand another person or group to further the relationship with them.

variations.name: third party social knowledge
variations.description: Participating in social knowledge transfer about someone not present to further a different relationship. Also known as 'gossip'.

variations.name: collecting knowledge
variations.description: Collecting knowledge of a favorite type can help people feel a sense of expertise, perhaps contributing to a sense of self-worth or social status.

variations.name: knowledge signaling
variations.description: You may seek a certain type of knowledge in anticipation of sharing it with a particular social group.

variations.name: discovering knowledge
variations.description: A successful search for information may give better knowledge about the physical or social environment. May result in triumph or epiphany.

commentaries.quote: Gossip and tabloids fill a need to understand what's considered important and scandalous.
There are experts on everything from celebrities to old beer cans to particle physics.

conditions: Perception that additional knowledge a certain type would be useful for a particular social reason.
Perception that additional knowledge a certain type is would be useful for survival or comfort.

1.description: Part of the brain may perceive the gap in knowledge as an opportunity or threat, and anticipate a chemical reward if gap is resolved.
